description: Altair WinProp as installed with Feko 2026.1: the ProMan, WallMan, TuMan, AMan and CompoMan applications, the WinPropCLI batch runner, the propagation models, network planning, result and database file formats, and the WinProp C/C++ API. Entries were checked against the installed binaries, HTML help and API headers.

tools.name: ProMan (Propagation Manager)
tools.description: ProMan is the main WinProp application. It holds the simulation project, runs every propagation model for rural, urban, indoor, tunnel and time-variant scenarios, runs the network-planning modules, and displays and evaluates results. You start a project with File > New Project, where you choose Propagation Analysis or an air interface (.wst), the scenario and the geometry databases. Almost everything else is set in Project > Edit Project Parameter.
tools.usage: ProMan.exe (Feko bin folder): File > New Project -> Project > Edit Project Parameter (Simulation / Propagation / Computation / Sites / Air Interface / Network / Traffic / Database tabs) -> Computation > Propagation (RUN PRO), Computation > Network Simulation (RUN NET) or Computation > Run All Computations

parameters.name: Wireless Technology
parameters.description: Propagation Analysis (no network planning possible) or a network-planning air interface, usually loaded from a .wst file.

parameters.name: Scenario
parameters.description: Rural/suburban, urban, indoor, tunnel or time-variant. The scenario decides which databases and propagation models are offered.

parameters.name: Databases
parameters.description: Topography and clutter (.tdb/.mdb), urban vector data (.odb, or pre-processed .ocb/.oib/.opb), indoor vector data (.idb, or pre-processed .idi etc.).

parameters.name: Polarimetric Analysis
parameters.description: Standard uses total gain only and works with all models. Full uses angle-dependent polarisation from .ffe patterns and works only with SRT, IRT and multi-wall with Fresnel/UTD.

parameters.name: Simulation tab
parameters.description: Prediction area (lower-left/upper-right corners), resolution and prediction heights. You can change these only if the database was not pre-processed in area mode.

parameters.name: Propagation tab
parameters.description: Result folder and the result types to compute (power, field strength, path loss, delay spread, propagation paths, ...).

parameters.name: Computation tab
parameters.description: Selects the propagation model and its settings. The models offered depend on the scenario.

tools.example:
1. File > New Project: Wireless Technology = Propagation Analysis, Scenario = Indoor, database = office.idb
2. Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab: Dominant Path Model
3. Propagation tab: choose a result folder and tick Power, Path Loss, Delay Spread
4. Project > Sites > Site: New, then add a transmitter with antenna pattern router_FF3D.ffe
5. Computation > Propagation and inspect results in the tree / 2D / 3D view
tools.notes: After project creation ProMan asks for a display height. This only affects the 2D display, not the prediction heights, and you can change it later with Display > Change Height in Display. IRT needs a database that was pre-processed in WallMan before you select it. Use WinPropCLI for headless runs. Do not launch the GUI from automation. Menu paths verified in the installed 2026.1 help (user_guide/proman).

tools.name: ProMan.exe command-line mode
tools.description: You can start ProMan with a project file and a computation switch so it loads and computes an existing project automatically. The first argument is the .net project, followed by one mode: -p propagation, -m mobile-station post-processing (RunMS), -n network, or -a all. Optional switches can come in any order. Unlike WinPropCLI, this still starts the ProMan application.
tools.usage: ProMan.exe <project.net> -p|-m|-n|-a [-fa] [-d<dB>] [-l] [-c] [-t <project.net> [<settings.mic>]]

parameters.name: -p
parameters.description: Compute the wave propagation prediction.

parameters.name: -m
parameters.description: Compute the mobile station prediction using RunMS.

parameters.name: -n
parameters.description: Compute the network prediction.

parameters.name: -a
parameters.description: Compute wave propagation, then RunMS (if enabled), then the network prediction.

parameters.name: -fa
parameters.description: Filter prediction results during computation using an arithmetic mean.

parameters.name: -d20
parameters.description: Limit the dynamic range of base-station antenna patterns, here to 20 dB.

parameters.name: -l
parameters.description: Write a computation log file.

parameters.name: -c
parameters.description: Close ProMan after the tasks finish successfully.

parameters.name: -t
parameters.description: Run RunMS post-processing with extra transmitter settings from a .mic file. Needs existing propagation results. If no .mic file is given, the project's default .mic file is used.

tools.example:
ProMan.exe C:\Projects\Office\office.net -a -l -c
ProMan.exe C:\Projects\Office\office.net -m -t C:\Projects\Office\office.net C:\Projects\Office\mimo4x4.mic -c
tools.notes: Only one computation mode is allowed per call. If none or several are given, ProMan runs the wave propagation prediction. The default .mic file has the same name as the project. Prefer WinPropCLI for cluster or queue runs because it needs no GUI. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help (Run From Command Line).

tools.name: WinPropCLI
tools.description: WinPropCLI runs ProMan projects, WallMan database pre-processing and binary-to-ASCII result conversion in batch mode, with no GUI, on Windows and Linux. It calls the WinProp API internally and works under queuing systems such as Altair PBS, Torque, LSF and GridEngine. -F with -P/-M/-N/-A computes the propagation, RunMS and network parts that are enabled in the project. The MPI build, WinPropCLI.impi, runs under Intel MPI (mpiexec) to spread standard ray tracing over processes and hosts.
tools.usage:
WinPropCLI -F <project.net> [-P|-M|-N|-A] [--multi-threading N] [--results-pro DIR] [-L] [-S d|g|a]
WinPropCLI -I <file.pin|file.pre> [-D <name>]
WinPropCLI -R <binary result file> [--res-out <name>]
mpiexec -n <procs> [-machinefile <file>] WinPropCLI.impi -F <project.net> -A --multi-threading <threads>

parameters.name: -F [ --file-project ] arg
parameters.description: Project file (.net) to compute.

parameters.name: -P [ --run-pro ]
parameters.description: Compute the propagation.

parameters.name: -M [ --run-ms ]
parameters.description: Compute the mobile-station post-processing (RunMS).

parameters.name: -N [ --run-net ]
parameters.description: Compute the network planning.

parameters.name: -A [ --run-all ]
parameters.description: Compute all modes enabled in the project (same as --run-pro --run-ms --run-net).

parameters.name: --multi-threading arg (=-1)
parameters.description: Number of computation threads.

parameters.name: --dynamic-limit arg (=-1)
parameters.description: Limit the dynamic range of base-station antenna patterns.

parameters.name: --filter-results arg (=-1)
parameters.description: Apply an arithmetic filter to prediction results during computation.

parameters.name: --results-pro / --results-ms / --results-net arg
parameters.description: Override the propagation / post-processing / network result directories. Paths are absolute or relative to the project file. If empty, the project's own directories are used.

parameters.name: --disable-project-update
parameters.description: Do not update the ProMan project files after computation.

parameters.name: -I [ --process-db ] arg
parameters.description: Database pre-processing from a .pin (indoor) or .pre (urban) parameter file. Give the path including the extension.

parameters.name: -D [ --db-out ] arg
parameters.description: Name of the resulting database, without extension. Defaults to the input file name.

parameters.name: -R [ --convert-res ] arg / --res-out arg
parameters.description: Convert a binary result file to WinProp ASCII format, optionally with a new output name (without extension).

parameters.name: -S [ --show-progress ] arg
parameters.description: Progress display: d = detailed per thread, g = global, a = automatic (default).

parameters.name: -L [ --log-create ]
parameters.description: Write log files during -P, -M, -N and -A runs.

parameters.name: -V [ --version ] / --help
parameters.description: Print the version (2026.1.0-8642 on this machine) or the option list.

tools.example:
"C:\Program Files\Altair\2026.1\feko\bin\WinPropCLI.exe" -F D:\wp\City\City.net -A --multi-threading 8 -L -S g
WinPropCLI.exe -I D:\wp\City\City_IRT.pre -D City_IRT
mpiexec -n 2 "C:/Program Files/Altair/2026.1/feko/bin/WinPropCLI.impi.exe" -F D:/wp/Office/Office.net -A --multi-threading 4
tools.notes: Options captured from the installed 2026.1 binary with WinPropCLI.exe --help. The binary spells -L as --log-create and uses --results-net, while the help page shows -results-net with one dash. The binary also has -C/--db-format database conversion (see 'WinPropCLI: database conversion'). If a GUI feature is not yet in the API, WinPropCLI reports an error: compute the propagation with WinPropCLI and run the network part in ProMan. For MPI, only Intel MPI is supported. Run initfeko first, and list per-host process counts in the machinefile as host1:2. The WinProp GUI tools are Windows-only; WinPropCLI also runs on Linux.

tools.name: WinPropCLI: database conversion (-C / --db-format)
tools.description: The installed WinPropCLI can also convert geometry and map data to WinProp formats: -C <file> with a numeric --db-format code, the same converter IDs that the API function WinProp_Convert uses. Codes 1-20 are topography, 101-114 clutter (morpho), 201-218 urban building data and 301-319 indoor/3D geometry. Run with --db-format-help to print the full list.
tools.usage:
WinPropCLI -C <source database file> --db-format <code>
WinPropCLI --db-format-help

parameters.name: -C [ --convert-db ] arg
parameters.description: Path of the database file to convert.

parameters.name: --db-format arg
parameters.description: Input format code. Topography: 2 .tdb, 3 .tdi, 4 ASCII grid .asc, 14 USGS DEM, 15 USGS BIL, 16/17 HGT, 18 DTED, 19 GeoTIFF. Clutter: 104 .asc, 113 GeoTIFF. Urban: 201 .oda, 203 .gml, 204 MapInfo .mif/.tab, 205 Arcview .shp, 206 AutoCAD .dwg/.dxf, 216 OpenStreetMap .osm, 217 .odb to .idb, 218 CityGML. Indoor: 301 .ida, 302 .dwg/.dxf, 303-305 .stl, 306 Nastran .nas, 307 .obj, 308 .fac, 310 IFC, 312 .3ds, 313 .fbx, 314 .blend, 315 glTF, 316 COLLADA .dae, 317 .idb to .odb, 318 CityGML, 319 OpenDRIVE .xodr.

parameters.name: --db-format-help
parameters.description: Print every supported format code, grouped as TOPO, MORPHO, URBAN and INDOOR.

parameters.name: -D [ --db-out ] arg
parameters.description: Name of the resulting database without extension. The help text does not say whether it applies to -C as well as -I.

tools.example:
WinPropCLI.exe --db-format-help
WinPropCLI.exe -C D:\maps\campus.osm --db-format 216
WinPropCLI.exe -C D:\cad\factory_hall.ifc --db-format 310
tools.notes: -C, --db-format and --db-format-help exist in the installed 2026.1 binary, but the WinPropCLI help page does not describe them. The code list was captured by running WinPropCLI --db-format-help. The 2026.1 release notes fix .shp conversion in WinPropCLI. The 2026 notes add material assignment when converting urban data to ASCII .oda. WallMan's shapefile converter needs the matching .dbf (building heights) next to the .shp. The API header additionally lists 202 = Vector Data ASCII (.vda) for WinProp_Convert.

tools.name: WallMan (vector database editor)
tools.description: WallMan is the graphical editor for WinProp vector building databases. It creates and edits urban (.odb) and indoor (.idb) databases, converts CAD/GIS and topography data, and assigns materials, vegetation, courtyards/towers, time-variant object groups and prediction planes. It also runs the database pre-processing that intelligent ray tracing needs. Pre-processing projects (.pre urban, .pin indoor) are created with File > New Project and computed with Preprocessing > Compute Current Project.
tools.usage: WallMan.exe: File > New Database | File > Convert Urban Database | File > Convert Indoor Database | File > Convert Topo Database | File > New Project -> Preprocessing > Edit Preprocessing Parameters -> Preprocessing > Compute Current Project

parameters.name: File > Convert Urban Database
parameters.description: Import modules for .oda, Arcview .shp (+ .dbf heights), MapInfo .mif/.mid, AutoCAD .dwg/.dxf, GML/CityGML, OpenStreetMap .osm and several vendor formats. Can simplify buildings during import.

parameters.name: File > Convert Indoor Database
parameters.description: Imports .ida, .dwg/.dxf, .stl, .nas, .obj, .fac, .ifc, .gml/.citygml, .3ds, .fbx, .blend, .gltf/.glb, .dae and OpenDRIVE .xodr into an .idb.

parameters.name: File > Convert Topo Database
parameters.description: Topography converters: .tdb/.tdi, ASCII line and grid, binary grid, USGS DEM/BIL, HGT, DTED, Planetary Data System, GeoTIFF, vendor formats.

parameters.name: Mode of Preprocessing
parameters.description: Empirical vertical plane models, Intelligent Ray Tracing (3D, or 2x2D variants) or Urban Dominant Path. The mode decides the output file (.ocb/.oib/.opb for urban; .idc/.idw/.idi/.idp for indoor).

parameters.name: Edit > Launch Time Variant Mode
parameters.description: Assigns movement to object groups in indoor databases (ALD or RAC mode).

tools.example:
1. File > Convert Urban Database, format Arcview Shapefile, select city.shp (city.dbf in the same folder), save city.odb
2. File > New Project and select city.odb
3. Preprocessing > Edit Preprocessing Parameters: Mode = Intelligent Ray Tracing 3D, height 1.5 m, resolution 10 m, tiles/segments 60 m
4. Preprocessing > Compute Current Project -> city.oib, ready for ProMan
tools.notes: For IRT, the pre-processing fixes the prediction height and grid; you cannot change them later in ProMan. Scale databases to metric units (Objects menu) before pre-processing, because free-space losses are calibrated to metres. Do not give the output the same name as the input database, or the input is overwritten. File > Export > Export Project as ZIP Archive avoids absolute paths. The same pre-processing runs headless with WinPropCLI -I. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: TuMan (tunnel manager)
tools.description: TuMan is the graphical editor for tunnel and stadium geometries. You define tunnel tracks, cross sections (including junctions) and prediction planes, then export the geometry as a WinProp indoor database, either for ProMan directly or for further detail in WallMan. From the command line it can open a .tub project, export the tunnel as .ida (ASCII) or .idb (binary) and close again.
tools.usage: TuMan.exe [PROJECT.tub] [--export FILE.ida|FILE.idb] [-c | --close]

parameters.name: PROJECT
parameters.description: Full path of the TuMan project (.tub) to open.

parameters.name: --export FILE
parameters.description: Full path of the exported WinProp indoor database. Use .ida for ASCII or .idb for binary.

parameters.name: -c / --close
parameters.description: Close TuMan after opening (and exporting, if requested).

tools.example: TuMan.exe c:/Examples/Example1.tub --export c:/Indoor_Database/Example1.ida --close
tools.notes: TuMan file types: .tub (document with tunnel geometry and configuration), .csb (cross-section geometry), .sla (ASCII shape list of track elements), .mcb (global material database), and .ida/.idb exports. After export the workflow is the same as an indoor propagation project. 2026.1 adds a Ground Wall option in the Tunnel Wall group, which generates the ground as topography triangles. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: AMan (antenna pattern manager)
tools.description: AMan is WinProp's antenna-pattern editor and converter; it is not an antenna solver. It displays 2D and 3D patterns, converts vendor formats such as .msi/.pln and Huber+Suhner, and builds 3D patterns from horizontal and vertical cuts using four interpolation algorithms. You can also draw 2D patterns over a scanned data sheet, and generate antenna-array and 5G beam/envelope patterns. Results are saved as .apb/.apa or .ffe for ProMan.
tools.usage: AMan.exe: File > Open Antenna Pattern | File > Convert 2x2D to 3D | File > Convert MSI to 3D | File > Convert HuberSuhner2D to 3D | File > Antenna Array Tool | File > Convert to beams and envelope patterns | File > Generate beams and envelope patterns

parameters.name: File > Convert 2x2D to 3D
parameters.description: Interpolates a 3D pattern from WinProp binary 2D patterns (.ahb horizontal, .avb vertical only). You choose the algorithm and angle increments.

parameters.name: File > Convert MSI to 3D
parameters.description: Loads an .msi/.pln 2x2D pattern and interpolates it to 3D.

parameters.name: File > Antenna Array Tool
parameters.description: Rectangular array. Base element is isotropic, dipole or an external Feko .ffe unit cell. Amplitude taper can be uniform, triangular, cosine or Dolph-Chebyshev, in the XY or XZ plane. Writes an .ffe file.

parameters.name: File > Generate beams and envelope patterns
parameters.description: Builds 5G control/data beam patterns and their envelope from gains and beamwidths, and writes 5G-specific .ffe files for ProMan.

parameters.name: File > Convert to beams and envelope patterns
parameters.description: Combines existing per-beam pattern files (from simulation or measurement) into the 5G beam and envelope formats.

tools.example:
1. AMan: File > Convert MSI to 3D, select Kathrein741794.msi, pick an interpolation algorithm and increments
2. Check the 3D view, then save as .apb
3. In ProMan assign the .apb in the Sites > Cell dialog (Antenna Pattern)
tools.notes: AMan and ProMan read Feko .ffe patterns directly. The array tool writes its file but does not display it; open it with File > Open. The 2026.1 fix removes spikes in horizontal cuts of incomplete .ffe patterns. The MASC module (multiple antennas on masts) is also inside AMan. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: AMan: Multiple Antenna Scenario Configuration (MASC)
tools.description: MASC, built into AMan, computes the real radiation pattern of antennas mounted on masts, arms, tubes or walls, or behind radomes. It also handles several antennas fed with different powers and phases, such as quasi-omni configurations. The 3D scenario is generated from parameters, and the pattern is computed by superposing direct, reflected, diffracted and transmitted rays. The configuration is saved as an .ank project; the resulting pattern is saved separately.
tools.usage: AMan: File > New Multiple Antenna Config | File > Open Multiple Antenna Config | File > Save (.ank) | Multiple Antenna Config > Save Antenna Pattern | Multiple Antenna Config > Save Scenario (3D Indoor Data)

parameters.name: Main Settings
parameters.description: Global MASC settings. Confirming the main dialog with OK starts the computation.

parameters.name: Arms / Sub-Arms / Antennas / Radomes
parameters.description: Geometry, position, orientation (azimuth, tilt), materials and Tx power/phase of each element.

parameters.name: Mast / Wall configuration
parameters.description: Mounting structure whose reflection and transmission losses change the pattern.

parameters.name: Save Antenna Pattern
parameters.description: Writes the computed pattern (.apb) for ProMan or other planning tools; it can also be exported to formats such as .msi/.pln.

parameters.name: Save Scenario (3D Indoor Data)
parameters.description: Exports the generated mast/arm/radome objects in WallMan format for ray-tracing studies.

tools.example:
1. AMan: File > New Multiple Antenna Config
2. Define the mast, then add two arms with one sector antenna (.msi) each, at azimuth 0 and 120 deg
3. Confirm the main dialog with OK to compute
4. Multiple Antenna Config > Save Antenna Pattern -> site_combined.apb; File > Save -> site.ank
tools.notes: The .ank file stores only the configuration. You must save the computed .apb separately, or ProMan has nothing to load. The 2026.1 release fixes a MASC crash when several arms are at the same location. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: CompoMan (component catalog editor)
tools.description: CompoMan edits the component catalogs (.cpw) used by indoor network projects in ProMan. Components include antennas, cables, combiners, splitters, amplifiers and transceivers, each with manufacturer data and frequency bands. ProMan accounts for cable and component losses when it computes antenna outputs. In 2026.1 CompoMan can define MIMO transceivers and MIMO antennas with per-port patterns per frequency, XPD, .ffe patterns and per-pattern polarisation.
tools.usage: CompoMan.exe: create or edit components from the toolbar or main menu; Settings > Frequency Bands. In ProMan, use the Component toolbar (Add component / Add cable / Add antenna / Add transceiver) or Project > Edit Project Parameter > Components tab.

parameters.name: Component types
parameters.description: Antenna, cable, combiner, splitter, amplifier, transceiver, and similar RF parts, with technical and manufacturer details.

parameters.name: Settings > Frequency Bands
parameters.description: Editable list of bands. Assigning bands to components narrows the choice when adding them to a network project.

parameters.name: MIMO transceiver / antenna (2026.1)
parameters.description: MIMO configuration with antenna patterns per port and operating frequency.

tools.example:
1. CompoMan: add an antenna component, load its .ffe pattern and assign the 3.5 GHz band
2. Save the catalog (.cpw)
3. ProMan indoor network project: Component toolbar > Add antenna, pick it from the catalog, and connect cables to a transceiver
tools.notes: .cpw is listed as 'Components Catalog' in the native-file list. Components are only available in indoor network projects. Project components linked to a catalog update automatically when the catalog changes. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and release notes.

tools.name: ProMan: Auto Calibration (Models & Materials)
tools.description: Fits propagation-model parameters to measurement data. For some models it can also fit material or clutter properties. A prediction run with propagation paths enabled writes .cal calibration files, and the calibration tool then fits the model against measurement files in WinProp format (.fpp, .fpl, ...). Material calibration is available for indoor COST multi-wall, SRT and IRT; clutter calibration for rural empirical and deterministic two-ray.
tools.usage: ProMan: Computation > Auto Calibration (Models & Materials)

parameters.name: Measurement files
parameters.description: Measurements in WinProp result format, or ASCII data imported into a WinProp result.

parameters.name: Allow calibration of material
parameters.description: Checkbox in the Material Properties dialog (WallMan or the ProMan Calibration tool). It must be enabled for every material you want calibrated.

parameters.name: Propagation Paths
parameters.description: Additional Prediction Data option. It must be enabled so the prediction writes the calibration data.

tools.example:
1. Import drive-test data into a result of the same type (Import > Import Data)
2. Enable Propagation Paths under Additional Prediction Data and run the prediction (.cal files are written)
3. Computation > Auto Calibration (Models & Materials): select the measurements and the parameters to fit
4. Re-run the prediction with the calibrated model
tools.notes: The Feko bin folder also contains ProManCalibration.exe. The help calls it the 'ProMan Calibration tool', started from this menu, and documents no command line for it. The indoor one-slope, Motley-Keenan and DPM models have no material calibration. API alternative for DPM: WinProp_Calibrate_DPM(WinProp_Calib_DPM*). Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: ProMan: Dominant Path Model (DPM)
tools.description: A semi-deterministic model that finds only the dominant path between the transmitter and each pixel; that path typically carries more than 90 % of the energy, and the model is available for indoor, urban and rural scenarios. Path loss is the free-space term plus 10*p*log(l) plus accumulated interaction losses (and, indoors, wall transmission losses), minus a wave-guiding gain and the antenna gain. LOS/OLOS/NLOS path-loss exponents apply before and after a breakpoint. It needs no pre-processing, is fast and tolerates database errors, but it does not give the full channel impulse response.
tools.usage: ProMan: Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab > Dominant Path Model > Settings (Configuration of Dominant Path Model dialog). API: WinProp_Antenna.Model = WINPROP_MODEL_DPM (with Model_DPM) or WinProp_ParaMain.PredictionModelUrban = PREDMODEL_UDP / PredictionModelRural = PREDMODEL_RURAL_RDP

parameters.name: Path Loss Exponents
parameters.description: Exponents for LOS/OLOS/NLOS before and after the breakpoint. Higher values mean faster decay; use higher values when the database is missing many objects.

parameters.name: Losses
parameters.description: Maximum interaction (diffraction) loss per direction change; Auto (recommended) accounts for frequency.

parameters.name: Wave guiding
parameters.description: Empirical gain for propagation along corridors or street canyons, which models reflections without tracing them.

parameters.name: Transmission losses (indoor)
parameters.description: Wall penetration losses, accumulated along the dominant path.

tools.example:
1. File > New Project, Scenario = Urban, database Office_Park.odb (no pre-processing needed)
2. Computation tab: Dominant Path Model; Settings: LOS 2.0/3.0, OLOS 2.2/3.2 for a high transmitter
3. Computation > Propagation
API (urban): GeneralParameters.PredictionModelUrban = PREDMODEL_UDP; GeneralParameters.BuildingsMode = BUILDINGSMODE_UDP; // .opb database
tools.notes: Recommended exponents from the rural DPM table (before/after breakpoint): LOS 2.0/3.0 (high Tx) or 2.2/3.8 (low Tx); OLOS 2.2/3.2 or 2.3/4.0. Indoor guidance: p = 2.3 for furnished and 2.0 for empty buildings. Use ray tracing when you need delay spread, angular spread or the impulse response. Urban DPM can also use a WallMan-preprocessed .opb (UDP) database. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and headers (WP_Defines.h, OutdoorPlugIn_Defines.h).

tools.name: ProMan: 3D Intelligent Ray Tracing (IRT)
tools.description: A deterministic ray-optical model (reflections and diffractions, full multipath) for urban and indoor scenarios, sped up by a one-time WallMan pre-processing. Walls are split into tiles and wedges into segments, and their visibility relations are stored, so the prediction itself typically takes minutes. It gives path loss plus wideband results: delay spread, angular spread, impulse response and ray data. The pre-processing fixes the prediction height and grid.
tools.usage: WallMan pre-processing (Mode = IRT 3D or a 2x2D variant) -> .oib (urban), .idi (indoor) or .oib+.idi (hybrid CNP) -> ProMan: File > New Project with the pre-processed database -> Computation tab > Intelligent Ray Tracing. API: WINPROP_MODEL_IRT (indoor) / PREDMODEL_IRT with BUILDINGSMODE_IRT (urban)

parameters.name: Subdivision of Walls
parameters.description: Maximum tile size, horizontal and vertical. Suggested 40-100 m (typical 60 m) for urban. Smaller tiles mean longer pre-processing and larger files.

parameters.name: Subdivision of Wedges
parameters.description: Maximum horizontal and vertical segment size. Use smaller horizontal segments when over-rooftop diffraction dominates.

parameters.name: Enhanced Resolution Management
parameters.description: Adaptive-resolution factor, suggested 2 or 3.

parameters.name: Spheric Zone
parameters.description: Maximum distance for stored visibility relations, typically 600-1000 m (800 m fixed), or Auto (depends on element height).

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: 3D (reflections + diffractions); 2x2D with 2D-H IRT + 2D-V IRT; or 2D-H IRT + 2D-V knife-edge diffraction.

tools.example:
1. WallMan: File > New Project (city.odb) > Preprocessing > Edit Preprocessing Parameters: IRT 3D, height 1.5 m, resolution 10 m, tiles/segments 60 m
2. Preprocessing > Compute Current Project -> city.oib
3. ProMan: File > New Project, Scenario = Urban, database city.oib, Computation tab = Intelligent Ray Tracing
API: WinProp_Structure_Init_PreProUrban(&P); P.Model = PREDMODEL_IRT; P.Mode = PP_MODE_IRT_3D; OutdoorPlugIn_ComputePrePro(&P, "City_IRT_API", nullptr, nullptr, &Callback, nullptr);
tools.notes: Urban IRT needs knife-edge post-processing for hilly terrain. A hybrid prediction blends ray tracing with COST-Walfisch-Ikegami for pixels the rays do not reach. To enable optional SRT post-processing, set IRT_POSTPROCESSING_WITH_SRT y in the .nup/.nip file (it is off by default). The 2026.1 release fixes missing ground reflections when the Tx is outside the topography map. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and API examples.

tools.name: ProMan: 3D Standard Ray Tracing (SRT) and Shooting and Bouncing Rays (SBR)
tools.description: Two rigorous 3D ray models that need no pre-processing. SRT determines every path analytically: accuracy is very high, and run time grows with the number of walls and allowed interactions, especially diffractions. SBR launches rays instead and suits tunnels, where reflections are computed efficiently. Both give multipath results and, with Fresnel/GTD-UTD settings, support full polarimetric analysis with .ffe patterns; SRT is also the model parallelised by WinPropCLI.impi (MPI).
tools.usage: ProMan: Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab > Standard Ray Tracing or Shooting and Bouncing Rays. API: WinProp_Antenna.Model = WINPROP_MODEL_SRT or WINPROP_MODEL_SBR, with Model_RAYTRACING settings (WinProp_Structure_Init_Model_RayTracing)

parameters.name: Max. interactions
parameters.description: Maximum number of interactions per path (transmissions, reflections, diffractions). Raise it for corridors that turn several corners, at the cost of run time.

parameters.name: Fresnel / GTD-UTD
parameters.description: Physical reflection/transmission and diffraction coefficients. Required for Full polarimetric analysis and for writing the transmission matrix to ray files.

parameters.name: Propagation Paths output
parameters.description: Writes .str (ASCII) / .ray (binary) ray data for impulse-response, AoA/AoD and MIMO post-processing.

tools.example:
1. Indoor project on office.idb, Computation tab: Standard Ray Tracing, with Fresnel/UTD
2. Propagation tab: enable Delay Spread and Propagation Paths
3. Batch/MPI: mpiexec -n 4 WinPropCLI.impi -F office.net -A --multi-threading 4
tools.notes: Ray data can be written only when the project databases use UTM coordinates. For automotive radar, detailed vehicles can be replaced with simple objects plus Feko RCS (.ffe). Only Intel MPI is supported for WinPropCLI.impi. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and WP_Defines.h.

tools.name: ProMan: COST 231 Walfisch-Ikegami and ITU-R P.1411 urban models
tools.description: Two empirical urban models with very short run times. COST 231 (extended Walfisch-Ikegami) uses the transmitter and receiver heights plus the vertical building profile (mean building height, road width, building separation, road orientation). It is accurate above the mean rooftop level, does not model wave guiding, and covers 800-2000 MHz up to about 5 km. ITU-R P.1411 covers short-range outdoor links from 300 MHz to 100 GHz up to about 1 km, with four environment categories and site-specific or site-general sub-models.
tools.usage: ProMan (urban project): Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab > COST 231 Walfisch-Ikegami or ITU-R P.1411. API: WinProp_ParaMain.PredictionModelUrban = PREDMODEL_COST (BUILDINGSMODE_COST loads an .ocb) or PREDMODEL_ITU1411 (Model_UrbanITU1411)

parameters.name: Propagation Environment (P.1411)
parameters.description: Urban very high rise, urban/urban high rise, suburban/urban low rise, or residential.

parameters.name: Propagation Models (P.1411)
parameters.description: Site-Specific uses the buildings in the urban database. Site-General uses only general environment properties and antenna height, so the database can be almost empty.

parameters.name: LOS / NLOS (COST 231)
parameters.description: The model treats LOS street-canyon links and NLOS over-rooftop links differently.

tools.example:
1. File > New Project, Scenario = Urban, database city.odb
2. Computation tab: COST 231 Walfisch-Ikegami
3. Computation > Propagation
API: GeneralParameters.ScenarioMode = SCENARIOMODE_URBAN; GeneralParameters.PredictionModelUrban = PREDMODEL_COST;
tools.notes: COST 231 accuracy drops for transmitters below the mean rooftop level, and neither model is recommended for hilly terrain. COST 231 is the empirical partner in hybrid ray-tracing predictions, and in the Getting Started hybrid urban/indoor example it is combined with DPM. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and OutdoorPlugIn_Defines.h.

tools.name: ProMan: Knife Edge Diffraction model
tools.description: A vertical-plane diffraction model that evaluates the knife edges formed by buildings (vector data) or clutter heights, plus the terrain profile. It suits large distances and satellite links where ray tracing is too costly. It is an urban prediction model (PREDMODEL_KE) and also serves as an additional knife-edge diffraction step that adds hill shadowing to rural empirical models.
tools.usage: ProMan: Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab (knife edge model or additional knife edge diffraction) -> Parameters for Additional Knife Edge Diffraction dialog. API: PREDMODEL_KE

parameters.name: Model for computation of additional diffraction loss
parameters.description: Method used to find knife edges and the resulting extra loss.

parameters.name: Maximum number of diffractions
parameters.description: Caps the number of knife edges considered per prediction.

parameters.name: Diffractions at clutter objects
parameters.description: Set automatically by ProMan (display only) when the clutter database includes clutter heights.

tools.example:
1. Rural project with Topo.tdb and a clutter .mdb, Computation tab: Okumura-Hata
2. Enable additional knife edge diffraction, maximum 3 diffractions
3. Compute and check the shadowing behind ridges
tools.notes: In 2026.1 the urban knife-edge diffraction losses were aligned with the empirical diffraction losses of the default material properties (maximum loss and out loss). WallMan pre-processing keeps the building data of the whole area, so knife-edge post-processing stays possible after IRT. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and release notes.

tools.name: ProMan: indoor empirical models (One Slope, Motley-Keenan, COST Multi-Wall)
tools.description: Fast indoor models based on the direct ray; none needs pre-processing. One Slope (modified free space) is a rough estimate that ignores walls, and Motley-Keenan adds one uniform loss per wall crossed (L = LFS + Lc + kw*Lw). COST 231 Multi-Wall uses each wall's own material loss plus a floor term with an empirical correction. None of them models reflection, diffraction or wave guiding.
tools.usage: ProMan (indoor project): Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab > One Slope / Motley-Keenan / COST Multi-Wall. API: WinProp_Antenna.Model = WINPROP_MODEL_FREESPACE / WINPROP_MODEL_MOTLEYKEENAN / WINPROP_MODEL_COST231 (Model_FREESPACE / Model_MOTLEYKEENAN / Model_COST)

parameters.name: Uniform transmission loss (Motley-Keenan)
parameters.description: Single wall loss for all walls, set with the Settings button.

parameters.name: Wall and floor losses (Multi-Wall)
parameters.description: Per-material wall losses and a floor loss. These are fitted model coefficients rather than physical losses, so they implicitly include furniture.

parameters.name: Fresnel/UTD (Multi-Wall)
parameters.description: Multi-wall with Fresnel coefficients/UTD is allowed with Full polarimetric analysis.

tools.example:
1. Indoor project on office.idb
2. Computation tab: COST Multi-Wall
3. Compute, then compare with DPM to see the missing corridor wave-guiding
tools.notes: Multi-wall supports material calibration, and the optional .idc pre-processed database belongs to it. Motley-Keenan ignores individual materials. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help (indoor model summary) and WP_Defines.h.

tools.name: ProMan: rural empirical models (Okumura-Hata, Empirical Two-Ray, ITU-R P.1546, ITU-R P.525/P.526)
tools.description: Fast rural/suburban coverage models on topography with optional clutter. Okumura-Hata (optionally with the Hata extension) is valid for 30 MHz-3 GHz, Tx 30-200 m, Rx 1-10 m and 0.1-40 km, and Empirical Two-Ray combines direct and ground-reflected rays with propagation exponents. ITU-R P.1546 is a point-to-area method for land/sea paths from curves with location-probability corrections. ITU-R P.525 & P.526 combines free-space loss with terrain-profile diffraction (modified Deygout plus spherical Earth).
tools.usage: ProMan (rural project): Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab. API: WinProp_ParaMain.PredictionModelRural = PREDMODEL_RURAL_HATA / PREDMODEL_RURAL_2RAY_EMP / PREDMODEL_RURAL_ITU1546 / PREDMODEL_RURAL_ITU526

parameters.name: Clutter table
parameters.description: Per-class losses and heights used by Hata and the two-ray models.

parameters.name: Location probability (P.1546)
parameters.description: Field strength exceeded at q % of locations, using the local ground-cover spread.

parameters.name: Additional knife edge diffraction
parameters.description: Adds hill shadowing, which Hata, ETR and P.1546 otherwise ignore.

tools.example:
1. File > New Project, Scenario = Rural/Suburban, Topo.tdb + clutter .mdb
2. Computation tab: Okumura-Hata, with knife edge diffraction enabled
3. Computation > Propagation
API: GeneralParameters.ScenarioMode = SCENARIOMODE_RURAL; GeneralParameters.PredictionModelRural = PREDMODEL_RURAL_HATA;
tools.notes: The P.1546 page states 30-3000 MHz and 1-1000 km, while the rural summary table says 30 MHz-4 GHz and 0.1-1000 km. P.526 ignores ground electrical properties and reflections. Empirical Two-Ray supports clutter calibration. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and OutdoorPlugIn_Defines.h.

tools.name: ProMan: Longley-Rice (ITM) and Deterministic Two-Ray models
tools.description: Two 2D vertical-plane rural models. Deterministic Two-Ray (DTR) computes the direct and ground-reflected rays ray-optically and superposes them coherently or by power. Longley-Rice (Irregular Terrain Model) predicts long-term median loss over irregular terrain from 20 MHz to 40 GHz over 1-2000 km, mainly for broadcast frequency planning. It has a point-to-point mode (uses the terrain profile) and an area mode (uses empirical medians).
tools.usage: ProMan (rural): Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab > Deterministic Two Ray / Longley-Rice (Parameters of ITM dialog). API: PREDMODEL_RURAL_2RAY_DET (Model_DetTwoRay) / PREDMODEL_RURAL_ITM (Model_RuralITM)

parameters.name: Radio Climate (ITM)
parameters.description: One of seven predefined climate regions.

parameters.name: Electrical Properties (ITM)
parameters.description: Ground permittivity and conductivity, either from defaults (Use Default Values) or from the clutter table.

parameters.name: Reliability / Confidence (ITM)
parameters.description: Statistical levels for time/location variability and prediction confidence.

parameters.name: Superposition (DTR)
parameters.description: Coherent or power superposition of the direct and ground-reflected rays.

tools.notes: For ITM, clear 'Consideration of curvature of earth surface' on the Pixel Databases tab. DTR supports clutter calibration. The example code is from the installed rural_propagation API example, which runs DTR through OutdoorPlugIn_ComputePrediction. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and API examples.

tools.name: ProMan: Parabolic Equation (PE) model
tools.description: A full-wave 2D vertical-plane model that numerically solves the standard parabolic equation over terrain. Reflection, diffraction and forward scattering are handled implicitly, together with ground conductivity and permittivity (optionally height-dependent permittivity). It is accurate but has long run times, and is often used in aerospace and defence coverage studies.
tools.usage: ProMan (rural): Project > Edit Project Parameter > Computation tab > Parabolic Equation. API: PREDMODEL_RURAL_PE with Model_RuralPE (WinProp_Structure_Init_Model_RuralPE)

parameters.name: Ground conductivity / permittivity
parameters.description: Soil electrical properties; the page lists three ways to define them.

parameters.name: Start distance r_ini
parameters.description: The computation starts at a distance where propagation angles stay within +/-15 deg of the horizon, the validity range of the PE.

parameters.name: Absorbing layer
parameters.description: An absorbing medium (about 150 wavelengths) below the upper boundary suppresses artificial reflections.

tools.example:
1. Rural project with Topo.tdb
2. Computation tab: Parabolic Equation, ground properties from the clutter table
3. Compute and compare with Okumura-Hata (the help has a Hata vs PE comparison page)
tools.notes: Expect much longer run times than empirical models. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and OutdoorPlugIn_Defines.h.

tools.name: ProMan: leaky feeder cable models (SDM, STL, SPL)
tools.description: Models for radiating (leaky feeder) cables in buildings, tunnels and mines, where the power along the cable drops from the feed point according to the defined losses. Shortest Distance (SDM) uses the shortest distance from cable to receiver, with wall transmission losses and optionally the angle of incidence. Smallest Transmission Loss (STL) and Smallest Path Loss (SPL) split the cable into discrete sources and keep the path with the smallest transmission loss or path loss.
tools.usage: ProMan: Project > Site > Site: New, then choose the leaky feeder cable type in the Transmitter Type dialog. Draw the cable with the mouse or import its coordinates from ASCII. Model settings are in the Parameter for Prediction of Radiating Cables dialog.

parameters.name: Cable discretisation
parameters.description: Spacing of the discrete transmitting points for STL/SPL.

parameters.name: Angle dependency / path loss exponents
parameters.description: Apply to all radiating-cable models.

parameters.name: Cable losses
parameters.description: Longitudinal loss along the cable, defined on the Cell Definition tab.

tools.example:
1. Tunnel project on tunnel.idb exported from TuMan
2. Project > Site > Site: New, type leaky feeder cable; draw it along the tunnel ceiling and set the z-coordinates
3. Select STL, set 1 m discretisation, then compute
tools.notes: The mouse tool works only while the Edit Project Parameter dialog is closed. The API header also defines cable model IDs WINPROP_MODEL_ID_CABLE_SDM/STL/SPL/DPM. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and WP_Defines.h.

tools.name: ProMan: time-variant scenarios
tools.description: Time-variant scenarios cover moving vehicles, trains, doors, elevators or robots. Moving object groups are defined in WallMan on an indoor database; ProMan then uses the scenario 'Time-Variant Scenarios (3D vector data with non-stationary objects)' and computes the time samples you select. A transmitter can be stationary or move with an object group. If only the Tx/Rx move, trajectories are defined in ProMan and no WallMan time variance is needed.
tools.usage: WallMan: Edit > Launch Time Variant Mode (choose ALD or RAC) -> ProMan: File > New Project, Scenario = Time-Variant -> Project > Edit Project Parameter > Simulation tab (time samples)

parameters.name: ALD mode
parameters.description: Absolute distances; rotation follows the direction of motion. Intended for vehicles on streets or rails.

parameters.name: RAC mode
parameters.description: Relative distances; rotation set by length or angle and direction. Intended for doors, elevators and robots.

parameters.name: Time samples
parameters.description: Time instances to compute, set on the Simulation tab.

parameters.name: Trajectories
parameters.description: Paths for moving transmitters or prediction points defined in ProMan, with an optional velocity profile (enables Doppler).

tools.example:
1. WallMan: group the car faces, Edit > Launch Time Variant Mode > ALD, define the path and speed, then Leave
2. ProMan: New Project > Time-Variant, attach the radar Tx to the car group
3. Simulation tab: 0-2 s in 0.5 s steps; use SRT; compute
API example: api/winprop/examples/indoor_propagation_timevariant
tools.notes: Time variance works only with indoor databases (.idb) and object groups, and the ALD/RAC choice cannot be changed later. You cannot edit or save in time-variant mode; leave it first. 2026.1 shows the time step in the 3D view and fixes ASCII export of only the first time step. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: ProMan: import radar cross-section (RCS) from Feko
tools.description: Speeds up ray-optical radar simulations by replacing detailed objects (for example cars) with a simple geometry plus monostatic or bistatic RCS computed in Feko and written to an .ffe file. Whenever a ray hits the object, ProMan uses the RCS to find the scattered field and corrects for finite distance. The RCS is assigned to an object group, which may be moving, in a time-variant project.
tools.usage: Feko: plane-wave excitation with an angular sweep plus a far-field request ('Calculate fields in plane wave incidence direction' on for monostatic, off for bistatic), then Advanced tab > Output fields to ASCII file (*.ffe). ProMan: Project > Edit Project Parameter > Database tab > Monostatic or bistatic radar cross-section (RCS) > Add a new RCS dialog

parameters.name: RCS origin
parameters.description: Defaults to the centre of the group's bounding box. You can adjust it, often the Z-coordinate to match the radar height.

parameters.name: Azimuth adjustment
parameters.description: Aligns the object orientation between Feko and WinProp. With X = East, the spherical coordinates are identical.

parameters.name: Averaging filter
parameters.description: Smooths high-frequency RCS that varies by many dB within a few degrees.

parameters.name: Incidence tolerance
parameters.description: Bistatic data is used within 10 deg of the pre-computed incidence angles.

tools.example:
1. CADFEKO: car model, plane wave with theta/phi sweep, far-field request with 'Calculate fields in plane wave incidence direction'; export car_mono.ffe
2. WallMan: model the car as a simple box group in the time-variant .idb
3. ProMan: Database tab > Add RCS, choose car_mono.ffe, assign it to the car group, then run SRT
tools.notes: Monostatic RCS contains only backscatter, so it is not suitable for vehicle-to-X communication. The 2026.1 release fixes bistatic RCS .ffe files with one theta sample, and 2025.1 improved single-incidence-direction RCS. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: Feko .ffe antenna patterns in AMan and ProMan
tools.description: The main Feko-WinProp coupling: design the antenna in Feko, export its far field to an .ffe file in POSTFEKO, then use it directly as a transmitter or receiver pattern in ProMan, or open and convert it in AMan. With Standard polarimetric analysis only the total gain is used. With Full analysis the separate theta/phi patterns and polarisation are used, but only with SRT, IRT and multi-wall with Fresnel/UTD. Feko .ffe files also feed the AMan array tool, AMan 5G beams, RCS import and (from 2026.1) CompoMan.
tools.usage: POSTFEKO: export far field -> farfield_gain_3d.ffe. ProMan: File > New Project > Polarimetric Analysis (Standard | Full) -> Project > Edit Project Parameter > Sites > Cell dialog > Antenna Pattern > select the .ffe (Directional / Sector antenna)

parameters.name: Standard polarimetric analysis
parameters.description: Uses the total gain. Polarisation direction and cross-polar level are set per transmitter and applied uniformly over the pattern.

parameters.name: Full polarimetric analysis
parameters.description: Angle-dependent polarisation for Tx and Rx from the .ffe (or an .ffe written by AMan).

parameters.name: Downtilt / azimuth
parameters.description: Orientation of the pattern in the Cell dialog.

tools.example: Getting Started example 2: export the base-station sector pattern from POSTFEKO as farfield_gain_3d.ffe, assign it in ProMan to each cell with a 4 deg downtilt, then solve with DPM and COST 231.
tools.notes: The .ffe format itself is documented in the Feko User Guide (Summary of Files > Far Fields). The antenna gain shown in the Cell dialog is the maximum gain read from the file. Also see 'AMan: antenna pattern formats'. Verified in the installed 2026.1 WinProp help (getting started GS1/GS2, AMan, ProMan pages).

tools.name: ProMan: network planning project (air interface .wst, RUN NET)
tools.description: Network planning is post-processing on top of a propagation run. You create the project with an air-interface definition, usually a predefined wireless-standard file (.wst), and first compute the received power of every transmitter (RUN PRO). RUN NET then does cell assignment and computes SNIR, data rate, throughput, coverage probability and more. Multiple-access schemes include FDMA, TDMA, CDMA/WCDMA/HSPA, OFDM/SOFDMA (FDD/TDD), UWB and 5G.
tools.usage: ProMan: File > New Project (select a .wst air interface, scenario, databases) -> Project > Edit Project Parameter (Air Interface, Simulation, Traffic, Network, Propagation, Sites, Components tabs) -> Computation > Propagation: Compute All -> Computation > Network Simulation. Export an interface with File > Export > Export Air Interface Properties (*.wst)

parameters.name: Air Interface tab
parameters.description: Carriers (number, bandwidth, separation), transmission modes / modulation and coding, required SNIR, duplex (FDD/TDD), MIMO scheme and cell-assignment settings.

parameters.name: Simulation tab
parameters.description: Area, resolution and heights, plus the simulation approach: static (homogeneous or clutter-based traffic) or Monte Carlo.

parameters.name: Network tab
parameters.description: Folder for network results and which network result types to compute.

parameters.name: Traffic tab
parameters.description: Cell load and traffic definitions per application.

tools.example:
1. File > New Project: Wireless Technology = LTE .wst, Scenario = Indoor, database office.idb
2. Sites tab: three transmitters on different carriers
3. Computation > Propagation: Compute All (RUN PRO), then Computation > Network Simulation (RUN NET)
4. Inspect SNIR, Best Server, Max Throughput
Batch: WinPropCLI -F office.net -A
tools.notes: A project created as Propagation Analysis cannot run network predictions. Share network projects as the .net file plus its .nip/.nup/.nrp file. Defining a custom air interface is recommended only for experienced users. 2026.1 makes RunNet much faster for trajectories with many samples. The API equivalent is WinProp_Net_Project_Open_WST. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: ProMan: cell assignment and Monte Carlo traffic simulation
tools.description: Cell assignment is the first step of every network computation. For each receiver pixel, a carrier counts as received if it meets the minimum SNIR and, optionally, the minimum power, and a selection mode picks the serving cell. A Monte Carlo network simulation places individual users randomly according to location-dependent traffic and repeats snapshots until cell loads converge. The report counts served, not assigned, traffic-blocked and quality-blocked users per application and cell.
tools.usage: ProMan: Project > Edit Project Parameters > Air Interface tab > Cell Assignment; Project > Edit Project Parameter > Simulation tab (Monte Carlo approach); Monte Carlo report in the network results

parameters.name: Selection Mode
parameters.description: Highest Rx power among the carriers received; highest Rx power of all carriers in the network; highest SNIR among the carriers received; or highest SNIR of all carriers in the network.

parameters.name: Minimum Required SNIR
parameters.description: Always applied. Can be negative.

parameters.name: Minimum Required Power
parameters.description: Optional additional power threshold.

parameters.name: Handover
parameters.description: Trajectory mode only: switch cells only when the new cell is better by the handover offset (dB) for longer than the time to trigger (ms).

parameters.name: Monte Carlo states
parameters.description: Served, Not assigned (coverage hole), Blocked (traffic: no free resources), Blocked (quality: insufficient Rx power or SNIR).

tools.example:
1. Air Interface tab > Cell Assignment: Highest Rx power among carriers received, min SNIR -5 dB
2. Simulation tab: Monte Carlo, 10 snapshots; Traffic tab: user density per clutter class
3. RUN NET, then read the Monte Carlo report (last snapshot and average), DL power load and UL noise rise per transmitter
tools.notes: Pixels without a serving cell stay uncomputed (white) in the cell-area map. Fix coverage holes with more sites, traffic blocking with more carriers or smaller cells, and quality blocking by reducing interference. API: WinProp_Net_NetworkMonteCarloStats_Get, and the monte_carlo_5g example. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: ProMan: MIMO (network planning and RunMS post-processing)
tools.description: WinProp models MIMO in two ways. In network planning, you select the MIMO scheme (up to 8x8) on the Air Interface tab and assign each base-station element a carrier, signal group and MIMO stream; results include MIMO streams and data rates. Alternatively, you run a propagation with an isotropic Tx and saved propagation paths, then define real antenna arrays at both ends as post-processing (RunMS). That gives, for example, channel capacity in bits/s/Hz.
tools.usage: Network: Project > Edit Project Parameter > Air Interface tab > MIMO Technology + Settings. Post-processing: Computation > Propagation Postprocessing incl. Tx and Rx > Edit Parameters > Start Computation (batch: WinPropCLI -M or ProMan.exe -m)

parameters.name: Signaling Overhead
parameters.description: Applied once for 2x2, 1.5 times for 3x3, twice for 4x4, and so on up to four times for 8x8.

parameters.name: Beam forming
parameters.description: Phase-weighted transmission of the same signal to maximise received power. It can be combined with spatial multiplexing.

parameters.name: Antenna arrays (RunMS)
parameters.description: Base- and mobile-station arrays with imported .ffe/.apa/.apb element patterns, positions and orientations; coherent or incoherent ray combination (Channel Data tab).

tools.example:
1. Propagation tab: request Propagation Paths; Tx isotropic; RUN PRO
2. Computation > Propagation Postprocessing incl. Tx and Rx > Edit Parameters: 4-element ULA at the BS, 2 elements at the MS
3. Start Computation, then open the channel capacity result (.cap)
tools.notes: Because RunMS is post-processing, you can compare several array designs without re-running the propagation. 2026.1 speeds up RunMS by up to 4x, adds a vertical uniform linear array option, and renames the dialog to 'Settings of the Base and Mobile Station Antenna Arrays' on the Base Station tab. API: C++ class WinProp_SuperposeMS (source/SuperposeMS). Verified in the installed 2026.1 help, release notes and headers.

tools.name: ProMan: propagation result files (.fpp, .fpl, .fpf, .fpd, .los, .str, .ray)
tools.description: Per-transmitter wave-propagation results that ProMan writes to the result folder set on the Propagation tab, in WinProp's binary result format. Which types are available depends on the model: power, field strength, path loss, delay and delay spread, angular/elevation spread and means, LOS state, number of interactions, and ray data. Binary files can be converted to WinProp ASCII or exported as ASCII, grids or images.
tools.usage: ProMan: Project > Edit Project Parameter > Propagation tab (result folder + result checkboxes); File > Open Result. Batch conversion: WinPropCLI -R <file>

parameters.name: .fpp / .fpf / .fsl / .fpl
parameters.description: Received power, field strength (dBuV/m), field strength (linear) and path loss.

parameters.name: .fpd / .fpt
parameters.description: Delay spread and delay time.

parameters.name: .asb / .asm, .esb / .esm, .amb / .amm
parameters.description: Angular spread, elevation spread and angular mean at the BS and MS.

parameters.name: .los
parameters.description: LOS state: LOS, OLOS (indoor only), NLOS, LOS-V and NLOS-V (shadowed by vegetation or furniture).

parameters.name: .fpi / .fml
parameters.description: Number of interactions and morpho (clutter) loss.

parameters.name: .str / .ray
parameters.description: Ray data in ASCII (POINT/PATH keywords, impulse response, optional transmission matrix) and binary form.

parameters.name: .txt
parameters.description: ASCII export of arbitrary result data.

tools.example:
WinPropCLI.exe -R D:\wp\Office\PropResults\Tx1_Power.fpp --res-out Tx1_Power_ascii
API: WinProp_Result R; WinProp_Structure_Init_Result(&R); WinProp_Result_Read(&R, "Tx1_Power.fpp");
tools.notes: Ray data can be written only for UTM-based databases and cannot be displayed together with path-loss results. The transmission matrix is available only for indoor SRT with Fresnel and GTD/UTD. The binary format is not published; use WinPropCLI -R or WinProp_ConvertResultToASCII to get ASCII. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help (Types of Results, Native Files) and WP_Defines.h (PROP_RESULT_* enum).

tools.name: ProMan: network planning result files (.fpb, .cid, .mtd, .srp, .cap ...)
tools.description: Area results written by RUN NET to the folder set on the Network tab. They cover the serving cell and coverage, signal and interference levels, link quality, data rate and throughput, LTE measurements, MIMO and traffic. Each result type has its own extension, and ASCII export of any result uses .txt. The corresponding API constants are NET_RESULT_*.
tools.usage: ProMan: Project > Edit Project Parameter > Network tab (result folder + checkboxes) -> Computation > Network Simulation; File > Open Result

parameters.name: .fpb / .cid / .sid / .sig
parameters.description: Best server, cell area, site area, signal area.

parameters.name: .fpm / .spr / .oif / .din / .uin / .sin
parameters.description: Maximum received DL power, signal power, interference, interference+noise DL/UL, total received interference.

parameters.name: .mdr / .mdu, .mtd / .mtu, .dda / .dua, .atd / .atu
parameters.description: Maximum data rate DL/UL, maximum throughput DL/UL, data rate DL/UL, throughput DL/UL.

parameters.name: .srp / .srq / .ssi / .cqi
parameters.description: LTE RSRP, RSRQ, RSSI and CQI.

parameters.name: .ecd / .ecu, .ebn / .ebu, .rpb / .pro
parameters.description: Ec/Nt DL/UL, Eb/N0 DL/UL, reception probability.

parameters.name: .msd / .msu / .cap / .cov
parameters.description: MIMO streams DL/UL, channel capacity, coverage.

parameters.name: .hho / .sit / .fpn / .sho / .ast
parameters.description: Number of received carriers, sites and TRX; soft handover; active set size.

parameters.name: .exp / .fse / .pdy / .uds / .tfa .tfs .tfb .tfo
parameters.description: Exposure, exposure field strength, power density, user distribution, traffic analysis/served/blocked/offered.

tools.notes: The SNIR extension differs between help pages. 'Types of Results' lists SNIR as .fpc and SNR DL/UL as .snr/.snu, while the native-file list maps .sni to SNIR and .fpc/.snr to Interference. Check your result folder. EMF/EMC results follow the .emc specification (Data > EMC Specification). Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and WP_Defines.h (NET_RESULT_* enum).

tools.name: ProMan: radar signal processing (FMCW and pulse radar)
tools.description: Turns ray-based radar predictions into range-Doppler and range-angle heat maps and IQ data, using the same algorithms FMCW or pulse radar hardware uses. This shows the effect of algorithm limits and helps tune radar parameters. In 2026.1 the point cloud uses angle-of-arrival estimates from FFT and MUSIC, pulse radar supports AoA in azimuth and elevation, and vertical antenna arrays are supported.
tools.usage: ProMan: select Power (MS) or Power in the results tree -> Display > Radar > FMCW Radar -> click a radar result pixel -> FMCW Radar Postprocessing dialog (Set Radar Parameters or Design Radar Parameters)

parameters.name: Chirp duration
parameters.description: Sawtooth sweep period in microseconds. Sets the maximum measurable velocity and the velocity resolution.

parameters.name: Sweep Bandwidth
parameters.description: Difference between the chirp start and stop frequencies. Sets the maximum range and the range resolution.

parameters.name: Superposition of rays
parameters.description: Uncorrelated (power) superposition gives higher peaks and weaker ghost targets than coherent superposition.

tools.example:
1. Time-variant SRT project with a moving radar Tx/Rx (automotive_radar example)
2. Results tree: Power (MS); Display > Radar > FMCW Radar; click the radar pixel
3. Set chirp duration and sweep bandwidth, then view the range-Doppler map
API: C++ classes WinProp_FMCW_Radar / WinProp_Pulse_Radar (compute), example indoor_propagation_fmcw
tools.notes: The radar API classes are declared in source/Radar/FMCW/winprop_fmcw_radar.h and source/Radar/Pulse/winprop_pulse_radar.h. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help, release notes and headers.

tools.name: ProMan: export results and projects (ASCII, ASC grid, Google Earth, ZIP, report)
tools.description: ProMan exports result maps and whole projects for use in other tools. You can export results as ASCII tables or matrices, ESRI-style ASC grids, geo-referenced bitmaps, a Google Earth overlay (.kml plus image), DXF, XML or values along a polyline. A project can be packed with its patterns and databases into a ZIP archive with relative paths, and a Word report with one image per result can be generated. ASCII prediction data can also be imported into an existing result.
tools.usage: File > Export Data (Area) > Export ASCII | File > Export > Export Data (Area) > Export ASC Grid | File > Export Data (Area) > Export Google Earth | File > Export > Export Project as ZIP Archive | Project > Report Generator > Generate Result Report | Import > Import Data

parameters.name: Export ASCII
parameters.description: Export of Measurement Data dialog: header, table or matrix layout, handling of unpredicted pixels, data-block keywords.

parameters.name: Export ASC Grid
parameters.description: Header ncols, nrows, xllcorner, yllcorner, cellsize, NODATA_value, then values from the upper-left corner.

parameters.name: Export Google Earth
parameters.description: Image (.bmp, .jpg, .pcx, .png, .tga, .tif) plus a generated .kml overlay.

parameters.name: Export Project as ZIP Archive
parameters.description: Uses relative paths; options Export results and Export display settings. Only available when the project view is active.

tools.example:
1. Open the result Tx1 Power
2. File > Export > Export Data (Area) > Export ASC Grid -> Tx1_Power.asc for GIS
3. File > Export > Export Project as ZIP Archive (tick Export results) to hand the project to a colleague
tools.notes: Importing ASCII prediction data requires an open ProMan result of the same value type, and coordinates must match (they can be converted in the import dialog). N.C. marks not-computed values. 2026.1 fixes ASCII export of time-variant results, which previously exported only the first time step. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: WallMan: urban vector database (.odb / .oda)
tools.description: .odb (outdoor database binary) is WinProp's raw urban building database: 3D buildings as polygonal cylinders with materials, plus vegetation, virtual buildings, courtyards/towers and optionally embedded indoor buildings for hybrid CNP. .oda is the open ASCII form, exported from WallMan with File > Export > ASCII and converted back with converter 201. ProMan can use an .odb directly for DPM or COST; IRT needs the pre-processed .oib.
tools.usage: WallMan: File > Save As (.odb) | File > Export > ASCII (.oda). WinPropCLI -C city.oda --db-format 201 converts .oda to .odb. API: WinProp_Convert with ConverterID 201, BUILDINGSMODE_BINARY (.odb) / BUILDINGSMODE_ASCII (.oda)

parameters.name: Header (5 comment lines)
parameters.description: Lines starting with *, followed by the SETTINGS line.

parameters.name: SETTINGS
parameters.description: Number of buildings, offset x, offset y, extent x, extent y (a vector from the lower-left corner, not an absolute corner), info text. Building coordinates are relative to the offset and must be positive.

parameters.name: BEGIN_MATERIAL ... END_MATERIAL
parameters.description: Lines MATERIAL <id> GENERAL "name" thickness_cm filled R G B, and MATERIAL <id> FREQUENCY f_MHz eps_r mu_r sigma TLvert TLhor RL diff_in_min diff_in_max diff_out.

parameters.name: Buildings
parameters.description: Building records follow the material block. The building count must match SETTINGS, or WallMan reports an error.

tools.example:
* Urban Database
* Database generated by WallMan
*
*
*
SETTINGS 2087 0 5 2399.000 3392.000 WallMan
BEGIN_MATERIAL
MATERIAL 1 GENERAL "Material 1" 10.00000 1 0 0 0
MATERIAL 1 FREQUENCY 2000.000 4.000000 1.000000 0.010000 10.000000 20.000000 9.000000 8.000000 15.000000 5.000000
END_MATERIAL
...
tools.notes: Keep building coordinates below 10^6 and do not delete header lines. The API sample data folder ships City.oda/.odb/.oib/.opb. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help, API data and OutdoorPlugIn_Defines.h.

tools.name: WallMan: indoor vector database (.idb / .ida)
tools.description: .idb (indoor database binary) holds arbitrary 3D planar walls with materials and subdivisions (doors, windows), furniture and prediction planes. Some models can use it directly without pre-processing. WinProp uses 'indoor' for any geometry with full 3D freedom, so tunnels from TuMan, OpenDRIVE roads, CAD/mesh imports and time-variant scenes are also .idb. .ida is the ASCII form (Indoor Database ASCII).
tools.usage: WallMan: File > New Database / File > Convert Indoor Database / File > Save As (.idb). WinPropCLI -C hall.ida --db-format 301. API: WinProp_Scenario.VectorDatabase = "...idb" with WinProp_Open

parameters.name: Header
parameters.description: Any number of title or comment lines.

parameters.name: BEGIN_MATERIAL ... END_MATERIAL
parameters.description: Same MATERIAL GENERAL / FREQUENCY lines as the urban .oda format.

parameters.name: BEGIN_WALLS ... END_WALLS
parameters.description: Total number of walls, then one line per wall or subdivision. Comments inside the wall block must be enclosed in * signs.

tools.notes: Unlike urban databases, .ida has no offset. WallMan and ProMan report an error if the wall count is wrong. Converter 217/317 turns an urban .odb into an .idb and back. The 2026.1 release fixes .idb imports failing on duplicate wall IDs. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and API sample data (IndoorVectordatabase.ida/.idb/.idi).

tools.name: WallMan: pre-processed databases (.ocb, .oib, .opb, .idc, .idw, .idi, .idp) and .pre/.pin files
tools.description: WallMan pre-processing writes one binary database per mode, holding the checked building data, visibility information and the pre-processing parameters (area, resolution, heights). The parameter files are .pre for urban and .pin for indoor, and one raw database can have several of them. The pre-processed file you select in ProMan must match the propagation model.
tools.usage: WallMan: File > New Project (.odb or .idb) -> Preprocessing > Edit Preprocessing Parameters -> Preprocessing > Compute Current Project. Headless: WinPropCLI -I <file.pre|file.pin> [-D name]

parameters.name: .ocb
parameters.description: Outdoor COST binary, for empirical vertical-plane models (COST 231, knife edge).

parameters.name: .oib
parameters.description: Outdoor IRT binary, for urban intelligent ray tracing.

parameters.name: .opb
parameters.description: Outdoor UDP binary, for the urban dominant path model.

parameters.name: .idc / .idw / .idi / .idp
parameters.description: Indoor pre-processed files for COST multi-wall, standard ray tracing, intelligent ray tracing and indoor dominant path.

parameters.name: Hybrid CNP
parameters.description: .ocb + .idb or .oib + .idi, allowing urban-to-indoor and indoor-to-urban transitions.

parameters.name: .log
parameters.description: Optional pre-processing log (Generate log-file during pre-processing), named after the output database.

tools.example:
WinPropCLI.exe -I D:\wp\OfficePark\OfficePark_CNP.pre -D OfficePark_CNP_IRT
-> OfficePark_CNP_IRT.oib + .idi for a hybrid urban/indoor IRT project in ProMan
tools.notes: The urban pre-processing always stores the building data of the whole .odb area, so knife-edge post-processing stays possible. For IRT you can restrict the pre-processed area. A CNP project needs an .odb that contains at least one imported indoor database. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help.

tools.name: WinProp topography and clutter databases (.tdb, .tdi, .mdb, TDA ASCII)
tools.description: Rural and urban predictions use raster topography (digital elevation model) and clutter/land-usage databases. Topography is stored as .tdb (topo data binary), optionally tiled with a .tdi index file that points to files named xy_column_line.tdb. Clutter (morpho) data is stored as .mdb and may be split into several files. Heights are always in metres and pixels are square.
tools.usage: ProMan: Data > Topography Database | Data > Clutter (Morpho) Database > Convert | Data > Clutter (Morpho) Definition Table. WallMan: File > Convert Topo Database (for example > ASCII Line format). WinPropCLI -C <file> --db-format 1-20 (topo) / 101-114 (clutter)

parameters.name: .tdb / .tdi
parameters.description: Single topo database, or an index file with tiles. The .tdi is optional, and .tdb files are often used alone.

parameters.name: .mdb
parameters.description: WinProp clutter database, with class properties in the clutter definition table.

parameters.name: TDA ASCII line format
parameters.description: One pixel per line: East (longitude) North (latitude) Elevation (m), in UTM or geodetic coordinates, in any order.

parameters.name: Conversion options
parameters.description: Source coordinate datum, resolution, a height factor (0.30 for feet), interpolation of undefined pixels, and single vs index output for very large data.

tools.example:
1. ProMan: Data > Clutter (Morpho) Database > Convert, format ASC grid, source RuralClutter.asc -> Rural.mdb
2. WallMan: File > Convert Topo Database > GeoTIFF, DEM.tif -> Hilly.tdb
3. New rural project with Hilly.tdb + Rural.mdb
tools.notes: Supported non-native sources include .asc, .bin, USGS .dem/.bil, HGT, DTED .dt0-.dt5, GeoTIFF, Planetary Data System (.img/.lbl/.xml), .mda, and Nokia/MSI/Aircom/Agilent formats. If longitude and latitude resolutions differ, the smaller one is used for both. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and the WinPropCLI --db-format-help output.

tools.name: AMan: antenna pattern formats (.apb, .apa, .aha/.ava, .ahb/.avb, .msi/.pln, .ffe, .pat3d)
tools.description: The antenna pattern file types that AMan and ProMan read. .apb is the unpublished binary 3D format and .apa its ASCII equivalent. .ahb/.avb and .aha/.ava are horizontal/vertical 2D cuts in binary and ASCII. .msi/.pln are vendor 2x2D formats, .ffe is the Feko far field, and .pat3d is a Huber+Suhner 3D ASCII file.
tools.usage: AMan: File > Open Antenna Pattern. ProMan: Sites > Cell dialog > Antenna Pattern (.apb, .apa, .msi, .pln, .ffe). API: WinProp_Pattern.Mode = PATTERN_MODE_FILE; Filename = "...apb"

parameters.name: .apa layout
parameters.description: Lines starting with # or * are comments. Each data line holds theta (vertical) phi (horizontal) gain_dB [phase_deg], one direction per line, in any order and at any increment. Missing angles are interpolated.

parameters.name: .aha / .ava layout
parameters.description: After the comments, the first value is the number of pairs, then one 'angle gain' pair per line with no phase.

parameters.name: Gain convention
parameters.description: dB relative to an isotropic radiator: positive means gain, negative means attenuation.

parameters.name: PATTERN_MODE_2X2D / _3D / _FILE / _ANTENNA_ARRAY
parameters.description: API pattern modes in WP_Pattern.h.

tools.example:
* Theta Phi Attenuation
* Vertical Horizontal relative to iso
 0.00 0.00 -17.9900
 0.00 40.00 -17.9900
40.00 0.00 -19.3000
40.00 40.00 -20.4500
tools.notes: Convert 2x2D to 3D accepts only binary .ahb/.avb input; use Convert MSI to 3D for .msi/.pln. .msi is widely supported by other planning tools, and MASC results can be exported to .msi/.pln. .pln can also be an MSI Planet clutter file. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help and WP_Pattern.h. The '.ams' extension is not documented in the installed help and is left out.

tools.name: ProMan project files (.net with .nip/.nup/.nrp, .wst, .mic, .cpw)
tools.description: Saving a ProMan project writes the .net project file plus a scenario-specific parameter file: .nip for indoor, .nup for urban, .nrp for rural. You need both to share or batch-run the project. Related files are .wst (wireless standard / air interface definition), .mic (RunMS mobile-station settings), .cpw (component catalog), .emc (EMF/EMC limits), .ank (AMan MASC project) and .tub (TuMan project).
tools.usage: ProMan: File > Save Project -> office.net + office.nip; File > Export > Export Air Interface Properties (*.wst); File > Export > Export Project as ZIP Archive

parameters.name: .net
parameters.description: ProMan project file. This is the argument of WinPropCLI -F and ProMan.exe.

parameters.name: .nip / .nup / .nrp
parameters.description: Indoor / urban / rural project parameters. Some expert switches live here, for example IRT_POSTPROCESSING_WITH_SRT y.

parameters.name: .wst
parameters.description: Air interface file: carriers, transmission modes, required SNIR, cell assignment and MIMO settings.

parameters.name: .mic
parameters.description: RunMS settings file used by ProMan.exe -t. The default has the project name.

tools.example:
office.net + office.nip  (indoor network project)
WinPropCLI.exe -F office.net -A --disable-project-update
tools.notes: Project files may contain absolute paths to databases and patterns. Use Export Project as ZIP Archive to move a project between machines. The API sample data ships UrbanAPI.net/.nup and airInterfaces/5G FDD.wst. Verified in the installed 2026.1 help (Getting Started example 5, file appendix) and API data folder.

tools.name: WinProp C API: examples and build (CMake)
tools.description: The WinProp API is a C/C++ interface for running WinProp simulations from other software, and WinPropCLI is built on it. Headers are in %FEKO_HOME%\api\winprop\source (Interface, Net, Public, Radar, SuperposeMS, Beams). Import libraries are in api\winprop\export\winprop\64 (Engine, EngineConvert, EngineMS, EngineNet, EngineAI, InterMan, WPAPI2Proj), with the DLLs in %FEKO_HOME%\bin. Ready-made CMake examples cover indoor, outdoor, rural, network planning, 5G Monte Carlo/TDD, IRT pre-processing, database conversion, FMCW radar and time-variant cases.
tools.usage: cmake-gui: source = %FEKO_HOME%\api\winprop\examples\indoor_propagation, build = ...\indoor_propagation\Build -> Configure (Visual Studio generator) -> Generate -> Open Project -> build -> add %FEKO_HOME%\bin to PATH -> run

parameters.name: Prerequisites
parameters.description: Feko 2026.1, Microsoft Visual Studio 2015 or later, CMake 3.13 or later, and a license (set ALTAIR_LICENSE_PATH if you get a license error).

parameters.name: Compile definitions
parameters.description: The example CMakeLists define _WINPROP_API_ and _DLL_ENGINE_IMPORT and include source and source/Public.

parameters.name: Examples
parameters.description: indoor_propagation(_points/_timevariant/_fmcw/_movinggroups), outdoor_propagation(_openmp/_runms), rural_propagation, network_planning(_parallel/_5g_tdd), monte_carlo_5g, irt_preprocessing(_urban/_urban_CNP), convert_database, api.cpp, api.cs, apismall.cpp.

tools.example:
cd "%FEKO_HOME%\api\winprop\examples\indoor_propagation"
cmake -S . -B Build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64
cmake --build Build --config Release
set PATH=%FEKO_HOME%\bin;%PATH%
"%FEKO_HOME%\api\winprop\bin\APIExampleCPPIndoorPropagation.exe"
tools.notes: The example CMakeLists use relative paths (../../export, ../../source, ../../data) and write executables to api\winprop\bin. Under C:\Program Files you therefore need write access, or copy the whole api\winprop tree to a writable folder. Results go to api\winprop\data\output. On Linux the examples link libEngine.so. Paths and library names verified in the installed 2026.1 API folder and help (appendix/api).

tools.name: WinProp_Open / WinProp_Close (API)
tools.description: WinProp_Open creates a wave-propagation project handle for a scenario and loads its databases (vector database, and for rural cases pixel topography and clutter). It also registers progress, message and error callbacks. Every WinProp_Predict* call uses this handle, and WinProp_Close releases it. Like the rest of the API, both functions return 0 on success and an error code otherwise.

parameters.name: DataID
parameters.description: Output: handle of the new project.

parameters.name: DataScenario
parameters.description: WinProp_Scenario: Scenario (WINPROP_SCENARIO_URBAN / _INDOOR / _RURAL), VectorDatabase, PixelBldDatabase, TopographyDatabase, ClutterDatabase, ClutterTable.

parameters.name: DataCallback
parameters.description: WinProp_Callback with Percentage(int, const char*), Message(const char*) and Error(const char*, int) function pointers.

tools.notes: Declared in source/Interface/Engine.h (link Engine.lib). WinProp_Version(&major, &update, &bugfix, buf, size) returns the engine version. Always initialise structs with WinProp_Structure_Init_* before filling them. Verified in the installed 2026.1 headers and the indoor_propagation example.

tools.name: WinProp_Predict (API)
tools.description: Computes an area coverage prediction for one antenna in a project opened with WinProp_Open. It returns result matrices (power/field/path loss, delay, path type) and optionally ray matrices and results on prediction planes defined in the database. The propagation model comes from WinProp_Antenna.Model, and optional model settings are passed as a Model_* struct. Sister functions compute point receivers, arbitrary planes and trajectories.
tools.usage:
int WinProp_Predict(int DataID, const WinProp_Antenna *DataAntenna, const WinProp_Area *DataArea, const WinProp_Receiver *DataReceiver, int NrReceiver, const void *DataModelSettings, const WinProp_Additional *Additional, WinProp_Result **DataCoverageOut, WinProp_Result **DataDelayOut, WinProp_Result **DataNatureOfPathOut, WinProp_RayMatrix **DataRaysOut, WinProp_ResultPlaneList **PlanesResultOut, WinProp_RayMatrixList **PlanesRaysOut, const WinProp_Measurements *Measurements);
Also: WinProp_Predict_Points(...), WinProp_Predict_Planes(...), WinProp_Predict_Trajectories(...)

parameters.name: DataAntenna
